correctness.rationale: The norm-sum cubical join has maxima (T,U,1−T−U)~Dirichlet(p,q,1); conditionally one coordinate per block attains each maximum and other coordinates are independent uniform on its interval. Hence C=[(p+2)T²+(q+2)U²]/(3N), with mean from Dirichlet second moments. Independent Beta(p,q) split W=T/(T+U) and Beta(1,N) slack S give √N(W−p/N)→N(0,α(1−α)), NS→Exp(1). Conditional Lindeberg CLT for squared uniform coordinates yields noise variance (4/45)(α^5+(1−α)^5); the mean split variance is (4/9)α(1−α)(2α−1)^2, totaling (4/45)(1−15α²(1−α)²). At d=p−q~κ√N, expand exactly C=(1−S)^2[(N+4)/4+d(W−1/2)+(N+4)(W−1/2)^2]/(3N) and subtract the exact mean, giving (Z²−1+4κZ)/12−(E−1)/6; variance 1/24+κ²/9. No finite simulation substitutes for beta-Dirichlet and Lindeberg proofs.

value.rationale: The two block maxima are intrinsic canonical coarse radial coordinates; precisely at equal block sizes their linear Gaussian variance cancels and a different second-order law appears. This resolves a natural degeneracy, identifies the sqrt(N) imbalance scale, and distinguishes the full radius from conditional radial information, rather than promoting a routine moment calculation.

final_claim: Uniform Euclidean volume in a two-block cubical join yields a raw squared-radius CLT; the conditional radial-energy mean given both block maxima has a sqrt(N) imbalance crossover with a non-Gaussian quadratic-normal minus exponential limit.
limitations: Two orthogonal cube blocks with p/N→α in (0,1), non-Gaussian limit only for conditional mean; raw squared radius stays Gaussian.
